label: GEM well ID
purpose: Stable ID used by aggregations and target names.
details: Must be unique. Use the same value in aggregation_GEM_well_IDs.

label: Dataset
purpose: Groups related GEM wells for pre-aggregation summaries.
details: This is a processing and reporting group, not the donor identifier.

label: Donor ID
purpose: Links a non-multiplexed GEM well to donor metadata.
details: Use NA when donor identities will instead be resolved from a configured VCF.

label: Expected donors
purpose: States how many donors are expected in the GEM well.
details: Use 1 for an unmultiplexed well containing one donor.

label: Cell Ranger ARC count directory
purpose: Locates the Cell Ranger ARC count output for this GEM well.
details: Point to the directory containing outs, not to outs itself.

label: Use CellBender
purpose: Chooses whether corrected GEX counts replace the Cell Ranger counts.
details: When TRUE, the configured or standard-layout CellBender H5 file must exist.

label: CellBender H5 file
purpose: Optionally gives the corrected GEX count file.
details: Leave as NA when CellBender is disabled or its standard-layout path is used.

label: Donor VCF file
details: Without a VCF, every called nucleus receives GEM_well_donor_id.

label: Reference JSON
purpose: Identifies the exact Cell Ranger ARC reference used for count.
details: The genome must match the feature H5, and all GEM wells in an aggregation must use compatible references.

label: Pre-aggregation QC filters
purpose: Defines per-barcode filters applied before aggregation.
details: Write complete R expressions separated by ;;. An empty value applies no filters.

label: Active
purpose: Controls whether processing targets are constructed for this GEM well.
details: Every GEM well selected by an active aggregation must also be active.

label: Cell or nuclei sorting
purpose: Describes sorting or enrichment before library preparation.
details: Example optional metadata column for values such as sorted, depleted, or unsorted material. Add other GEM_well_ columns when your analysis needs them.
